Project: Kubernetes. Upgrade being assessed: 1.23 -> 1.29.
This change was introduced in release 1.28. Source: Kubernetes v1.28.0 CHANGELOG (official_changelog). Section: v1.28.0 / Changes by Kind / Deprecation.
Version facts from package metadata for this release (authoritative for version numbers): none

ITEM:
<<<
Changed kubectl version default output to be identical to what kubectl version --short printed, and removed --short flag entirely.
>>>

PARENT CONTEXT (same section, for disambiguation only):
<<<
v1.28.0 / Changes by Kind / Deprecation: Changed kubectl version default output to be identical to what kubectl version --short printed, and removed --short flag entirely. Kube-controller-manager deprecate --volume-host-cidr-denylist and --volume-host-allow-local-loopback flags. Kubelet: The --azure-container-registry-config flag has been deprecated and will be removed in a future release, please use --image-credential-provider-config and --image-credential-provider-bin-dir to setup acr credential provider instead. Removed tracking annotation from validation and defaulting. Removed withdrawn feature NetworkPolicyStatus. The deprecated flag --lock-object-namespace and --lock-object-name have been removed from kube-scheduler. Please use --leader-elect-resource-namespace and --leader-elect-resource-name or ComponentConfig instead to configure those parameters. KMSv1 is deprecated and will only receive security updates going forward. Use KMSv2 instead. In a future release, Set --feature-gates=KMSv1=true to use the deprecated KMSv1 feature.
>>>

Decide the disposition:
- "risk": the item describes something that can break an app/deployment, require migration work, or create operational risk.
- "context": it is accurate but needs no action at 1.29 (no user action required, deprecated-but-working, additive feature). Give the reason.

For "risk", produce one or more risk paths. Use separate paths for separate symbols/APIs when they can be checked independently. Hard rules:
1. Every condition has at least one quote copied EXACTLY, character for character, from ITEM or PARENT CONTEXT (contiguous span, 3-40 words, no ellipses, no added words). Do not fix typos or formatting.
2. Each path has exactly one condition with category "version" stating that the upgrade crosses release 1.28 (quote the text that ties the change to this release, or the change statement itself), and at least one application/deployment condition (category api_usage, configuration, dependency, runtime, deployment, database, behavior or test_coverage) describing what the app or deployment must use/have for the risk to apply.
3. If the text does not state something you need, do not assert it: use role "uncertain" and explain in ambiguities. derived_by: "extraction" when the text states the fact; for an application/deployment condition ("the application uses X"), use "extraction" when the text names X as the thing affected by the change. Use "inference" only when you infer an affected symbol, scope or impact that the text does not name. Only add ambiguities for real gaps or conflicts in the text, not for the general fact that a specific application has not been inspected.
4. role: "required" (must hold), "alternative" (any one of the alternatives suffices), "optional" (raises impact), "disqualifying" (if it holds, the risk does NOT apply, e.g. not using the new opt-in API), "uncertain".
5. operator/expected_value must be checkable: e.g. operator "present" with expected_value the literal symbol; "less_than" with a version; "equals" with a setting value. expected_value is a string.
6. If a replacement API/setting/version is named, put the migration step in suggested_actions and add a condition for any behavior that differs in the replacement when the text states one.
7. search_queries: for app-side conditions with a literal symbol, give ripgrep regexes (tool "ripgrep"), kubectl commands (tool "kubectl") or SQL (tool "sql") that would find usage. Empty list if no literal symbol.
8. primary_symbol: the most specific identifier of the change (full apiVersion string like "policy/v1beta1", setting name, function, flag, or runtime name like "Python"/"Node.js"). symbols: all identifiers involved.
9. risk_level rubric: critical = upgrade fails or data is at risk for most users meeting the conditions (e.g. unsupported runtime/database version, removed API version that stops serving); high = code or config meeting the conditions breaks at upgrade; medium = behavior change or migration with a clear workaround; low = edge case, cosmetic, or warning-only.
10. fires_at: "upgrade" (at upgrade time), "first_use" (when a feature is first exercised), "rotation" (on credential/password rotation), "rollout" (on deployment rollout), "future_removal" (deprecated now, removed later).
11. applies_to: fill upgrade_method (e.g. "pg_upgrade", "dump/restore"), cluster_type, or from_versions (a version specifier like "<3.1") ONLY if the text restricts applicability; otherwise null.
Do not output confidence.

paths.description: The --short flag of kubectl version was removed entirely in 1.28, and the default output of kubectl version now matches what --short previously printed. Scripts, CI jobs or tooling that invoke kubectl version --short will fail on an unknown flag, and those that parse the old default (long) output may see a different format.

conditions.statement: The upgrade from 1.23 to 1.29 crosses release 1.28, where the kubectl version --short flag was removed and the default output changed.
quotes: Changed kubectl version default output to be identical to what kubectl version --short printed, and removed --short flag entirely.
conditions.relevance: Ties the change to release 1.28, which is crossed when upgrading from 1.23 to 1.29.

conditions.statement: Scripts, CI pipelines, docs or tooling invoke kubectl version with the --short flag.
conditions.relevance: Invocations using the removed flag will fail after the kubectl client is upgraded to 1.28 or later.

conditions.statement: Scripts or tooling parse the default (non-short) output of kubectl version, whose format changed to match the former --short output.
conditions.expected_value: parsing of kubectl version default output
quotes: Changed kubectl version default output to be identical to what kubectl version --short printed
conditions.relevance: Parsers that depended on the previous long default output format may break.
ambiguities: The text does not describe the exact format difference between the old default output and the new one.

suggested_actions: Remove --short from all kubectl version invocations; the default output now matches the old --short output.
Review scripts that parse kubectl version default output and update them for the new format, or use structured output (e.g. -o json or -o yaml) where available.
Check the kubectl client version used in CI/automation after upgrading.
